real_qa.q: How does Homeworld Collective use AI to automate grant-making workflows with a tiny team?
real_qa.r: Homeworld Collective wired Claude with email history and standard operating procedures from Notion to create eight daily automated triggers that scan for grant extension requests and automatically draft responses when information is insufficient. When applicants provide the needed information, the system automatically drafts a contract and sends it through PandaDoc, with Paul reviewing and manually approving each draft before sending.

real_qa.q: What is the Jadgen frontier concept and how does it apply to using AI in startup operations?
real_qa.r: The Jadgen frontier, possibly coined by Ethan Mollick, describes the fact that AI is constantly changing and the frontier of what is available constantly shifts, bumping up against the frontier of what you know how to do and what you need to do. Part of working with AI is just doing it, and sometimes there are inefficiencies and sometimes there are great efficiencies, requiring constant learning about how your own context relates to an ever-shifting AI landscape.

real_qa.q: Why is AI ineffective at creating strategic documents from scratch and what is the dark side of AI-generated strategic content?
real_qa.r: AI is trained on the past so it cannot create the future; human cognition is the creator of the future and should use AI to weave together past context. When AI generates strategic content, it produces material that is just right enough to feel correct but wrong enough to be exhausting to fix, creating an uncanny valley effect where readers' brains turn off and assume it is true when it is actually wrong.
